title: vacation.rs: VacationResponse/get,set with singleton enforcement
description:
Implement VacationResponse/get and VacationResponse/set in src/vacation.rs.

## Methods to implement

### VacationResponse/get (RFC 8621 §8.1)
- Singleton: ids=["singleton"] or ids=null — always returns at most one object
- Fields: id (always "singleton"), isEnabled, fromDate, toDate, subject, textBody, htmlBody
- If no vacation response set: return empty list (not an error)

### VacationResponse/set (RFC 8621 §8.2)
- Singleton enforcement in handler layer:
  - Only "singleton" is a valid id for update/destroy
  - create with id="singleton" is NOT allowed — only update is
  - If client tries to create with a different id → invalidArguments error
- update: patch any field; isEnabled=false disables without deleting
- destroy "singleton": equivalent to disabling (isEnabled=false and clear body fields)
- Backend sees only get_objects / set_object calls — no singleton concept at backend level

## Key design decisions
- "singleton" id string is enforced in the handler, not the backend
- Backend stores at most one VacationResponse per account (keyed by fixed id "singleton")
- MemoryBackend: vacation_response: HashMap<AccountId, Option<VacationResponse>>

## Source references
- Stalwart (AGPL — read, do not copy): ~/GIT/stalwart-jmap-server/main/crates/jmap/src/vacation/
- RFC 8621 §8

## Test vectors
- Fresh account: VacationResponse/get → list.length=0
- VacationResponse/set create → invalidArguments error
- VacationResponse/set update singleton → VacationResponse/get returns it
- VacationResponse/set destroy singleton → get returns empty list again
